title: Introduce pluggable presubmit router and dependency allowlist harness
author: Maya Hernandez
release_notes: Adds a pluggable presubmit routing layer and an opt-in dependency allowlist to reduce presubmit churn and speed feedback. No behavioural changes to existing presubmit policies unless explicitly enabled.
description:
Context and motivation:
We continue to see noisy presubmit runs caused by transitive dependency updates and an increasingly monolithic presubmit graph. This PR introduces a lightweight, pluggable presubmit router and a dependency allowlist harness so teams can opt-in to narrower presubmit footprints and allow CI to skip expensive lint/test shards for allowed changes. The long-term goal is to decouple presubmit routing logic from monorepo-specific assumptions and make it easier to onboard targeted fast-feedback lanes.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces a presubmit router abstraction (infra/presubmit/router.go) that dispatches changes to configured lanes based on file globs, manifest hints, and dependency signals.
- Adds a dependency allowlist harness (pkg/ci/allowlist.go) that marks dependency-only changes as low-cost; teams can opt these into a slim presubmit path.
- Replaces the single presubmit workflow with a small composition layer in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml that wires the router to existing jobs.
- Adds small helper scripts and a lightweight base image for slim presubmit runs (ci/docker/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile, scripts/ci-slim-run.sh).
- Documentation and onboarding notes (docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md) and test coverage for the router logic (infra/presubmit/router_test.go).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The router is deliberately small: it evaluates a set of ordered rules and emits a route token. Complex route computation is deferred to future indexed heuristics to keep the initial roll-out safe and auditable.
- The allowlist harness uses package- and manifest-level heuristics (lockfile diff + manifest path mapping) to reduce false-positives. It is opt-in and can be disabled per-team via a config flag.
- We keep the full presubmit path intact and use the router only to select a smaller initial lane. Full tests run on merge to prevent regressions.

Checklist (what I tested locally / CI):
- Unit tests: router + allowlist (infra/presubmit/*_test.go)
- Integration smoke: presubmit workflow runs against a synthetic change set to validate routing decisions
- Verified fallback: when route resolution fails, we default to the existing monolithic presubmit to maintain safety
- Ran a canary rollout in the `contrib/ci-canary` team with the allowlist enabled for dependency bumps (observed ~48% reduction in average presubmit runtime for dependabot PRs)

Commits summary:
- 1f2a8c4: introduce presubmit router interface and rule evaluation engine
- 3b7d45a: implement file-glob + manifest rule sources and canonicalize input diff
- c9e012b: dependency allowlist implementation + allowlist config struct
- 6a4d2f0: presubmit workflow composition and slim runner image
- 5e9b3fa: docs, tests, and small infra fixes

Changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: compose router + existing jobs (small, explicit mapping)
- infra/presubmit/router.go, infra/presubmit/router_test.go: router implementation and tests
- pkg/ci/allowlist.go, pkg/ci/allowlist_test.go: allowlist harness and heuristics
- ci/docker/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile, scripts/ci-slim-run.sh: slim runner and invocation helper
- docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md: onboarding and operator notes

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Park (review): "Nice split — main question is safety. Can we make the allowlist conservative by default and require an explicit flag per team? Also suggest adding a debug header to the presubmit job showing which route was chosen."
- Maya (author): "Agreed. The allowlist is off by default; added `--allowlist-enabled` flag to team configs and a PRESUBMIT_ROUTE env var emitted by the router (see workflow)."
- Neha Singh (review): "Router looks good, but add more unit tests around lockfile diffs for yarn/pip/poetry cases."
- Maya: "Added additional lockfile diff fixture tests and a small note in docs describing heuristics and how to opt out."
- Liam O'Connor (approval): "Approach LGTM. Keep an eye on flaky route detection in the first week and we should surface route telemetry in the console."

CI status and reruns:
- Initial CI run: failed (flake in integration smoke due to ephemeral runner timeout)
- Re-run: pass across all checks (unit, integration-smoke, lint)
- CI notes: added a short timeout backoff to the presubmit smoke job to reduce noise (see commit 5e9b3fa)

Rollout and monitoring:
- Canary rollout completed for `contrib/ci-canary` and `infra-team` with allowlist opt-in; we observed a median presubmit runtime reduction of ~42-50% for dependence-only bumps in those teams.
- Added a route telemetry counter (instrumentation) that will be exposed in a follow-up PR to avoid inflating this change.

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. No migration required; behavior is opt-in and non-breaking. Teams can opt into router/allowlist via a repo-level config in `.presubmit-config.yaml` (sample in docs).

Follow-ups planned:
- Expose presubmit routing telemetry in Redwood Console for team-level adoption metrics (ENG-2301).
- Add an indexed rule backend for higher-accuracy route decisions and per-PR fast-path scoring (deferred to ENG-2359).

If you want to test locally:
- See docs/ci/presubmit-routes.md for a short recipe. Use `scripts/ci-slim-run.sh` to emulate a slim presubmit and `make presubmit-smoke` for the full canary workflow.

Contact:
- Author: Maya Hernandez (@mhernandez) — happy to walk through the router and assist with on-boarding teams.
